notes: Clear empty state: Bluetooth glyph, 'No barrier connected', one primary 'Connect to barrier' CTA.
Content block floats in the vertical middle with large empty areas above and below; the CTA would sit more naturally lower (thumb zone) or the block higher.
No secondary hint (e.g. 'Previously paired' or how to enroll a new barrier) for a first-time user; acceptable but thin.
'Not connected' pill is neutral grey; fine.
Hero reads instantly: flat arm, green tint, 'Lowered', plain sub-label.
Helper 'Already lowered.' explains the disabled Lower button: good.
Large dead band (~300 px) between guard chips and the pinned pad; the hero could take more of it or chips could sit closer to the pad.
Large title 'Barrier' plus subtitle 'M010-Barrier' repeats the word; DESIGN.md asks for the barrier name/nickname as the title.
State label has no glyph next to it (DESIGN.md 4.1 asks label + icon per state); the illustration carries it, so minor.
Best screen: moving arm, blue tint, elapsed '0.8 s of about 4.0 s' with progress bar, STOP promoted to filled danger, other moves disabled with 'Arm is moving. Use Stop.'
Large dead band (~300 px) between guard chips and the pinned pad; the hero could take more of it or chips could sit closer to the pad.
Progress track is thin (~6 px) and low-contrast against the tinted card; consider 8 px and a stronger track.
Upright arm, blue tint, 'Raised' with 'Your space is reserved.' read in under a second.
Lower button is filled green (success) while Raise is blue (accent): color follows destination state, consistent across screens.
Large dead band (~300 px) between guard chips and the pinned pad; the hero could take more of it or chips could sit closer to the pad.
Large title 'Barrier' plus subtitle 'M010-Barrier' repeats the word; DESIGN.md asks for the barrier name/nickname as the title.
Amber tint and 'Stopped' clearly separate it from Raising even though the arm angle is the same.
Both moves enabled and filled; STOP back to tonal: correct.
No helper line above the pad here, so the pad divider sits ~50 px lower than in other states; the layout jumps between states. Reserve the helper line height.
Large dead band (~300 px) between guard chips and the pinned pad; the hero could take more of it or chips could sit closer to the pad.
Banner copy is excellent: 'Can't move right now' / 'Something is in the way' / what to do, plus 'Safety checks' link and dismiss.
Zone chip flips to amber 'Zone blocked' in sync with the banner: good cross-referencing.

Hero still says 'Arm is flat. You can drive in.' directly above an obstruction warning; correct literally but reads as mixed signals. Consider muting the sub-label or appending 'Zone blocked' while the guard result is shown.
Banner sits only ~16 px above the move buttons and replaces the helper line; give it the 24 px section gap.
Light mode banner carries a drop shadow while the rest of the screen is flat (DESIGN.md: flat by default).
Fault is unmistakable: warning glyph + 'Fault' label, dashed arm, red tint, 'Controls locked.', on-site reset instruction.

Three red surfaces (hero, 'Sensors: see fault' chip, 'Needs on-site reset' card) compete; the hero sub-label 'Position sensors disagree' and the card body 'wrong end-limit switch fired' say the same thing twice in different words. Pick one wording and let the card carry the detail.
Card body text is visually heavier (black, body size) than its red title; consider title semibold and body secondaryLabel.
Dashed ghost arm and neutral card communicate 'unknown' well; 'Lower first to confirm position' and the single enabled Lower button guide the homing step.
The '?' glyph floats alone at the top of the card, detached from the label; place it inline with 'Position unknown' as Fault does.
Helper 'Lower first to confirm position' lacks the trailing period the other helpers use.
Large dead band (~300 px) between guard chips and the pinned pad; the hero could take more of it or chips could sit closer to the pad.
Fix confirmed: stale guard chips are gone while offline; only the 'Offline' pill, banner and dimmed hero remain.
Error first: 'Connection lost' + reassurance + full-width Reconnect is the right priority.
'Last known: Raising' with a mid-travel arm can still read as live motion at a glance; the faded stripes help. Add time since the last update (e.g. 'Not live - 12 s ago').
All three pad buttons go to the same neutral disabled style, so STOP loses its red identity; acceptable since the helper says 'Controls are off while offline.'
